## Decisions (with @rationale)

- `tile({"loop": "i", "factors": [32]})` :: Tile the outer i-dimension by 32 to create 512/32=16 outer tiles. This exposes parallelism across the 30 SMs on Ampere; 
- `tile({"loop": "j", "factors": [128]})` :: Tile j by 128 to create inner tiles of 128 elements. This aligns with 128-byte cache lines (32 fp32 elements) × 4 = 128-
- `parallel({"mapping": {"i": "threadblock.x"}})` :: Map the tiled i outer loop to threadblock.x so each block of 32 rows is processed by a distinct CUDA block. With 512/32=
- `parallel({"mapping": {"j": "warp"}})` :: Map the j tile loop to warps within each block. Each 128-element j-tile is handled by warps in lockstep — with 128/32=4 
- `vectorize({"loop": "j", "width": 4})` :: Vectorize the j inner loop with width 4 (float4 = 128 bits). This uses LDG.128 instructions, the widest load unit on Amp
